source:
Game Name (working title)
LAST ROUTE
"No one knows why the road is still open."
Core Idea
You and up to 5 friends are driving one truck across a frozen mountain to deliver the last generator core to a dying town.
Without it...
Thousands of people freeze.
So turning back isn't an option.
Core Gameplay Loop
Drive ⬇ Reach checkpoint ⬇ Random event ⬇ Solve it together ⬇ Repair truck ⬇ Continue ⬇ Repeat ⬇ Final escape
The truck almost never stops for long. The journey is the game.
The BIG Hook
The Storm Changes Every Run.
Not just weather.
The storm changes the world.
Examples:
🌨 Heavy snow.
Visibility 5 metres.
🧊 Frozen lake.
Road disappears.
Drive over ice.
Risk breaking through.
🌲 Fallen trees.
Need axes.
⛰ Avalanche.
New road opens.
Old road closes.
📡 Strange radio signal.
Follow it...
Or ignore it.
🏚 Abandoned village appears.
Sometimes.
Not every run.
Every run feels different.
Player Jobs
Everyone naturally gets a role.
🚛 Driver
Can only focus on driving.
🗺 Navigator
Uses map.
Finds routes.
Reads signs.
🔧 Mechanic
Repairs truck.
Keeps engine alive.
Changes tyres.
📦 Scavenger
Searches buildings.
Gets fuel.
Food.
Medicine.
Parts.
🔦 Lookout
Uses binoculars.
Warns about danger.
Nobody is standing around.
The Horror
No zombie waves.
No screaming monster.
Something...
Is following the truck.
It never attacks directly.
Instead...
Fuel disappears.
Doors open.
Lights go out.
Tyre tracks appear beside yours.
Someone knocks...
But nobody is there.
The mystery is the horror.
Mid Game Twist
You discover...
Every abandoned truck looks exactly like yours.
Same number.
Same cargo.
Same scratches.
How?
Nobody knows.
Now players start theorising.
Final Act
The storm gets insane.
Truck barely works.
Visibility almost zero.
Radio cuts in.
Someone says...
"Don't let it overtake you."
Now everyone panics.
You don't even know what "it" is.
Ending
Reach the town.
Unload generator.
Lights come on.
Storm instantly stops.
Outside...
Your truck has six sets of footprints around it.
Nobody says anything.
Game ends.
Players immediately start discussing what happened.
Why I think this is stronger
The mystery is what people remember.
Not:
"Big monster killed me."
But:
"WHY WAS THERE ANOTHER TRUCK?"
Those kinds of mysteries create YouTube theory videos.
MVP (cheap version)
One truck.
One mountain road.
Three checkpoints.
10-15 random events.
One ending.
No giant open world.
No massive AI.
The game could be finished in about 20-30 minutes per run.
But here's the one thing I'd still change.
I wouldn't make it a pure horror game.
I'd make it 70% adventure, 30% horror.
If players are scared the whole time, the fear wears off. If most of the game is about teamwork, driving, and making decisions, then the strange moments hit much harder because they're unexpected.
One last thing: if your goal is a viral Roblox game, don't try to beat Dead Rails by adding more monsters or more mechanics. Beat it by making players ask one question after every run:
"Wait... what actually happened out there?"
That kind of mystery gives people a reason to replay, tell their friends, and watch theory videos. That's much harder to copy than just another survival game.

image_prompt.text: A narrow winding mountain road climbing through the snow - the single directed route the truck follows, with no way back down
The dying town far below and ahead, and the mountain pass above, giving the drive a direction
The final descent out of the pass opening onto the town, so the layout itself reveals the destination
Fragile frozen lake crossings, avalanche debris, and fallen trees that punish careless driving
Abandoned village buildings off the roadside that players enter to scavenge
a heavy cargo truck on the road carrying a generator core
a surfaced route wide enough to drive a truck along, rather than a walking trail

layout_placement.text: Three checkpoints spaced along the climb where the run pauses for repair and a random event
Fuel, food, medicine and truck parts gatherable from the abandoned buildings
the town at the end of the road where the generator core is unloaded, ending the run

notes: No genre covers a co-op vehicle expedition where the truck is the mobile base and the world passes it; Adventure's guided corridor is the closest shape and it does not express the vehicle at all.
The storm rewrites the route mid-run - an avalanche closes the old road and opens a new one - which the handoff has no way to express; the emitted layout is one fixed route.
The stalking presence, the identical abandoned trucks, the player roles, and the ending are narrative and scripting with no spatial footprint.
Most of the prompt is pitch and design rationale rather than build instruction.

open_questions.ask: A mountain road with three checkpoints is a long strip - should it be one region-scale map, or three chapter maps joined at the checkpoints?
Should the abandoned village be a fixed location on the route, or does it need to be omittable since it only appears on some runs?

theme: Frozen mountain wilderness with restrained horror - heavy snow, dark pines, whiteout storm, muted cold palette

coverage_missing.ask: Does reaching the town need a build feature - an unload bay, a trigger volume - or is arrival purely scripted?
How long is the drive meant to feel? A 20-30 minute run at truck speed is far more road than one framed image can hold.
Are the alternate storm routes real branches in the map, or is one route swapped for another at runtime?

answers.ask: A mountain road with three checkpoints is a long strip - should it be one region-scale map, or three chapter maps joined at the checkpoints?
answers.answer: Use one compact region-scale mountain road with all three checkpoints along it. The MVP is one road and the journey should feel continuous, not split into separate chapter maps.

answers.ask: Should the abandoned village be a fixed location on the route, or does it need to be omittable since it only appears on some runs?
answers.answer: Make it omittable: it appears only on some runs as a random route-side event/location. It should not be a fixed required stop.
